Reference / os/account

os/account#

User() denotes the effective security identity of the current process.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let current = User();
let alice = User(name: "alice");
output.writeln(current.name(), " ", current.identity());

Description#

User() denotes the effective security identity of the current process. User(name: ...) denotes a named account. Construction only retains that choice; account information is requested lazily by name(), identity() and home():

identity() is deliberately opaque. A provider may use a decimal UID, a Windows SID or another stable account identifier; portable code compares or stores it only as a string. home() comes from the account database, not from HOME, USERPROFILE or another process-environment variable.
